english.title: Fail to take action required under Articles 40 or 41 of Regulation (EU) No 2016/425
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being an economic operator, failed to take the action required under Article

(A)_[40 of Regulation (EU) No 2016/425, relating to compliant PPE which presents a risk,]_
(B)_[41 of Regulation (EU) No 2016/425, relating to formal non-compliance,]_

in that **(..SPECIFY DETAILS..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 7(3) and 8 of the Personal Protective Equipment (Enforcement) Regulations 2018.

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required

Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Although these regulations revoked the Personal Protective Equipment Regulations 2002, the transitional provision in regulation 2(4) states that the 2002 Regulations continue to apply (as if they had not been revoked) to PPE placed on the market before 21st April 2019.
(ii) See also regulation 2(5) with regards to PPE which has an EC type-examination certificate issued under the 2002 Regulations.
(iii) Nothing in these regulations prevents the showing of PPE at trade fairs, exhibitions, demonstrations or the like, which is not in compliance with the provisions of EU Regulation 2016/425, provided that a visible sign clearly states that such PPE does not comply with those provisions and that it is not for sale until it is made compliant.
